concepts.def: Money that must be accepted for debts

walkthroughs.body_html:
UK coins: 1p, 2p, 5p, 10p, 20p, 50p, £1, £2.

UK notes: £5, £10, £20, £50. Since 2016 they are polymer (plastic) — harder to fake. 🪙

Royal Mint in Wales stamps the coins.

Bank of England in London prints the notes.

Both work hard to stop forgers — hidden threads, holograms, ink. 🔍

Legal tender means money that must be accepted to settle a debt.

In shops, a café can refuse a £50 note if they wish — sales aren't 'debts' in the legal sense.
